andhraPradesh.headline: AP issues G.O.Ms.No.244 to create promotion pathways for Ward Secretariat functionaries
facts: G.O.Ms.No.244 was issued by the Andhra Pradesh Municipal Administration & Urban Development Department on 27 September 2026.
The order sanctions 815 Junior Assistant posts by restructuring surplus posts, with no additional financial implication stated for this restructuring.
It approves upgrading 815 Ward Sanitation & Environment Secretary Grade-II posts and 815 Ward Planning & Regulation Secretary Grade-II posts to Grade-I.
Eligible Ward Administrative Secretaries may be considered for promotion to the new Junior Assistant posts; eligible Ward Data Processing Secretaries are next in the prescribed hierarchy.
andhraPradesh.summary: The State Government issued G.O.Ms.No.244 on 27 September, providing promotional channels for specified Swarna Wardu Sachivalayam cadres through post restructuring and upgrades. The order sanctions posts and sets out eligibility pathways; it does not itself announce that individual promotions have been completed.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Local government administration, civil-service promotion and cadre management
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: G.O.Ms.No.244 (MA&UD, 27 September 2026): 815 Junior Assistant posts and 815 upgrades each in two Ward Secretariat cadres.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess how structured promotion pathways and cadre restructuring can improve motivation and continuity in last-mile urban service delivery, while requiring transparent eligibility and implementation.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct Andhra Pradesh link: the order applies to Swarna Wardu Sachivalayams and functionaries in the State.

- **Coverage:** **Swarna Wardu Sachivalayams** in **Andhra Pradesh**.

# 2. **Posts and upgrades**
| Post / cadre | Approved change | Financial implication |
|---|---|---|
| **Junior Assistant** | **815 posts** sanctioned by restructuring surplus posts | No additional financial implication stated for the restructuring |
| **Ward Sanitation & Environment Secretary Grade-II** | **815 posts** upgraded to **Grade-I** | — |
| **Ward Planning & Regulation Secretary Grade-II** | **815 posts** upgraded to **Grade-I** | — |

# 3. **Promotion pathway**
- **Eligible Ward Administrative Secretaries:** May be considered for promotion to the new **Junior Assistant** posts.
- **Eligible Ward Data Processing Secretaries:** Next in the prescribed hierarchy.
- ⚠ **Trap:** The order creates promotional channels; it does not announce that individual promotions have been completed.
> Exam angle: **Date and year**—identify **G.O.Ms.No.244**, its issuing department and the **815** posts and upgrades.

andhraPradesh.headline: AP reviews flood inflows, advances barrage proposals and directs Hiramandalam lift-project action
facts: On 26 September, the Chief Minister reviewed heavy rain, flooding, river inflows and reservoir levels with senior officials.
Officials were directed to take forward proposals for two Krishna-basin barrages, including one between Pulichintala and Prakasam Barrage, and submit them to the Centre; these remain proposals.
Officials were directed to expedite power supply and complete lift works for the Hiramandalam Lift Project, and to facilitate diversion of Vamsadhara water into Hiramandalam Reservoir.
The review also directed free distribution of 50 kg of rice to each fisher family unable to go to sea for five days because of adverse weather.
andhraPradesh.summary: The 26 September review combined immediate flood-response directions with longer-term water-storage proposals. The barrages were not reported as approved or under construction, while the Hiramandalam directions concern expediting power connectivity and completing existing lift works.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: River-basin management, irrigation infrastructure and disaster response
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Distinguish a direction to advance barrage proposals from project approval or construction; Hiramandalam is linked to the Vamsadhara basin.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Examine how floodwater storage, irrigation operations and targeted relief can be coordinated, while balancing project appraisal, intergovernmental clearances and disaster risk.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct AP link: the proposals concern the Krishna basin and Prakasam Barrage, and the lift project and reservoir are at Hiramandalam in Srikakulam district.

# 2. **Water-project directions**

|---|---|

| **Hiramandalam Lift Project** | Expedite power supply and complete the lift works |
| **Vamsadhara water** | Facilitate diversion into **Hiramandalam Reservoir** |

andhraPradesh.headline: AP announces ₹11,085-crore Palle Panduga 3.0 rural-works programme
facts: On 27 September, the State announced that Palle Panduga 3.0 works worth ₹11,085 crore would be launched from Ramapuram village, Varikuntapadu mandal, Nellore district, on 29 September.
The announced components include 6,000 km of cement-concrete roads for ₹2,700 crore and 9,500 km of bitumen roads for ₹7,550 crore.
The plan also includes about 22,000 mini Gokulams (cattle sheds) for ₹300 crore, horticulture plantations over 50,000 acres for ₹225 crore, and 1,000 km of magic drains for ₹110 crore.
The 29 September launch was still scheduled at the time of the 27 September announcement; the works should not be treated as completed on this date.
andhraPradesh.summary: The Government announced a statewide rural-infrastructure programme and named Ramapuram in Nellore district as the launch venue for 29 September. On 27 September, the works were announced and scheduled, not yet launched or completed.

andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Palle Panduga 3.0 was announced at ₹11,085 crore; the 27 September report described a future 29 September launch.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how integrated rural roads, drainage, livestock and horticulture investments can support connectivity and livelihoods, alongside questions of funding, asset quality and maintenance.

andhraPradesh.headline: Food-safety operation across AP reports 25 closures and 30 cases
facts: Food Safety Department officials inspected 70 hotels, restaurants and other food establishments across Andhra Pradesh’s 28 districts on 26 September.
The operation resulted in 25 establishments being closed and 30 cases being registered; notices were issued to another 15 establishments.
Ten cases concerned establishments operating without valid food-safety licences; the remaining cases were reported as relating to unhygienic conditions.
Officials seized and destroyed more than 100 kg of cooked food reported unfit for consumption; the inspection report was published on 27 September.
andhraPradesh.summary: A statewide inspection drive reported enforcement action across all 28 districts, including closures, cases and notices. The reported violations included hygiene and food-storage concerns, making the operation relevant to public-health regulation and local enforcement.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Food safety regulation, public health administration and consumer protection
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The reported 26 September operation covered 28 AP districts; distinguish inspected establishments, closures, cases and notices as separate figures.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Evaluate how risk-based inspections, licensing, laboratory capacity and transparent compliance follow-up can strengthen food safety without relying only on episodic crackdowns.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct AP link: the reported inspection operation covered hotels and food establishments across all 28 districts of Andhra Pradesh.

- **Report:** Inspection report published on **27 September 2026**.

andhraPradesh.headline: Eastern Naval Command schedules 11th Vizag Navy Marathon for 13 December
facts: The Eastern Naval Command announced the 11th edition of the Vizag Navy Marathon for Visakhapatnam on 13 December 2026, as part of Navy Day celebrations.
The scheduled race categories are 42 km, 21 km, 10 km and 5 km; the route was reported as accredited by the Association of International Marathons and Distance Races.

national.headline: Tourism Ministry launches National Digital Tourism Stack and Dekho Apna Desh 2.0
facts: The Union Tourism Minister launched the National Digital Tourism Stack and the National Mission for Alternative Destinations—Dekho Apna Desh Campaign 2.0, on World Tourism Day.
The Digital Tourism Stack is being developed with ONDC and support from the International Centre for DPI Innovation and Advancement (ICDIA).
The shared digital infrastructure is intended to support discovery, payments, ratings and grievance redressal for tourism providers across participating platforms.
The Ministry said implementation would be phased, with a pilot planned for January 2027.
Dekho Apna Desh 2.0 aims to promote tourism-ready, lesser-known destinations and spread visitor demand more sustainably.
national.summary: Previous: World Tourism Day tourism-growth coverage was recorded earlier. Today: the Ministry launched the National Digital Tourism Stack and Dekho Apna Desh 2.0, adding concrete digital-infrastructure and alternative-destination initiatives to that topic. The pilot for the tourism stack is planned for January 2027.
national.staticLink: Digital public infrastructure; tourism-led inclusive and sustainable development; Centre–State coordination.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The National Digital Tourism Stack is being developed with ONDC; its stated pilot is planned for January 2027.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how interoperable digital infrastructure and promotion of lesser-known destinations can improve tourism access, local livelihoods and sustainable destination management.

- **Purpose:** Shared digital infrastructure for tourism providers across participating platforms
| Function | Use |
|---|---|

| Payments | **Payments** |
| Ratings | **Ratings** |
| Grievance redressal | **Grievance redressal** |

national.headline: India’s first LNG-powered train flagged off from Sabarmati
facts: The Union Home Minister flagged off the country’s first LNG-powered train from Sabarmati Railway Station, Ahmedabad, Gujarat.
The event also included the inauguration of railway development projects stated to be worth ₹1,472 crore.
The WAG-12 locomotive maintenance shed at Sabarmati was inaugurated; the PIB release stated its cost as ₹700 crore.
Kavach was introduced on the Sabarmati–Kalol–Sabarmati, Ahmedabad–Palanpur and Ahmedabad–Samakhiyali sections, according to the release.
national.summary: The first LNG-powered train was flagged off from Sabarmati on 27 September. The event also featured railway safety and infrastructure measures, including the introduction of Kavach on specified sections.

national.prelimsTakeaway: Sabarmati Railway Station in Ahmedabad was the departure point for the train described by the government as India’s first LNG-powered train.

international.headline: India calls for restraint, safe shipping and protection of civilians at UNGA 81
facts: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar delivered India’s statement at the 81st UN General Assembly General Debate in New York on 26 September.
India called for restraint, de-escalation, civilian protection and uninterrupted flows of energy and commerce amid conflicts.
Jaishankar highlighted attacks on commercial ships and seafarers across international waterways as unacceptable.
He described the Global South’s linked pressures as a “4F crisis”: food, fuel, fertiliser and finance.
India reiterated support for a two-state solution and said it would contribute to food and energy security.
international.summary: At the UNGA General Debate, India connected conflict de-escalation with civilian safety, maritime security and global energy and food flows. The address also highlighted economic vulnerabilities facing developing countries and India’s support for a two-state solution in West Asia.
international.staticLink: United Nations General Assembly; multilateral diplomacy; India’s foreign policy and maritime security
international.prelimsTakeaway: UNGA is the UN’s main deliberative, policymaking and representative organ; distinguish it from the Security Council’s primary responsibility for international peace and security.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss how India can combine strategic autonomy, maritime security, energy security and support for multilateral conflict resolution.

international.headline: Iran reiterates diplomatic path after US rejects proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
facts: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said diplomacy was the only way to resolve the conflict with the United States and Israel.
Iran’s proposal offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, subject to its conditions, and resume negotiations.
US President Donald Trump publicly rejected the proposal on 26 September.
The Strait of Hormuz is a strategic international waterway central to global energy transport.
The proposal remained unaccepted; no agreement to reopen the strait was reported.
international.summary: Iran maintained that a negotiated solution was necessary after the United States rejected its proposal concerning the Strait of Hormuz. The episode keeps energy-route security and the diplomatic management of conflict salient for countries, including India, that depend on stable international energy supplies.
international.staticLink: Strategic maritime chokepoints; energy security; diplomacy and conflict resolution
international.prelimsTakeaway: Locate the Strait of Hormuz between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman; it is a key route connecting Gulf energy exporters to the open sea.
international.mainsAngle: Assess how instability around maritime chokepoints can affect India’s energy security, trade and diplomatic choices.

- **What:** Araghchi said **diplomacy** was the only way to resolve the conflict with the **United States** and **Israel**
- **When:** Item dated **27 September 2026**; Trump publicly rejected Iran’s proposal on **26 September 2026**
- **Status:** **PROPOSED**; the proposal remained **unaccepted**

# 2. Strait of Hormuz proposal
- **Proposal:** Iran offered to reopen the **Strait of Hormuz within seven days**, **subject to its conditions**, and resume negotiations
- **Outcome:** No agreement to reopen the strait was reported
- **Location:** The **Strait of Hormuz** lies between the **Persian Gulf** and the **Gulf of Oman**

international.headline: India places 10th at WorldSkills Shanghai with six silver medals
facts: India finished 10th at the 48th WorldSkills Competition in Shanghai, China.
Indian competitors won six silver medals and 20 Medals for Excellence.

Silver medallists included Smriti Nambiar in Bakery and Mohammed Salam in Dental Prosthetics; four other Indian competitors won silver across digital design, industrial design, logistics and retail sales.
The six-day competition ran from 22 to 27 September and brought together more than 1,400 competitors from around 70 countries and regions.
India fielded 70 competitors across 63 skills; the Ministry described this as the country’s largest-ever WorldSkills contingent.
international.summary: India improved on its 13th-place finish at WorldSkills Lyon 2024, earning six silver medals and 20 Medals for Excellence in Shanghai. The results spotlight international benchmarking in vocational and technical skills and the performance of India’s skilled youth.
international.staticLink: Skill development; vocational education and training; human capital and employment
international.prelimsTakeaway: WorldSkills is an international vocational and technical skills competition; the 2026 Shanghai event was its 48th edition.
international.mainsAngle: Examine how international skills competitions can inform India’s vocational training, industry partnerships and employment-readiness policies.

international.headline: India wins combined-team trophy at Chess Olympiad; takes Open silver and Women’s bronze
facts: The 46th FIDE Chess Olympiad concluded in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on 27 September.
India won silver in the Open section and bronze in the Women’s section.
India received the Nona Gaprindashvili Trophy for the best combined performance across the two sections.
Uzbekistan won Open gold; China won Women’s gold.
India retained the combined trophy for a third consecutive edition; the next Olympiad is scheduled for the UAE in 2028.
international.summary: India finished the Samarkand Chess Olympiad with medals in both sections and retained the Nona Gaprindashvili Trophy for the best overall federation result. Uzbekistan won the Open title, while China topped the Women’s section.
international.staticLink: International sporting institutions; team competitions and sports governance
international.prelimsTakeaway: The Nona Gaprindashvili Trophy recognises the best combined federation result across the Open and Women’s Chess Olympiad sections.
international.mainsAngle: Consider how sustained international sporting performance depends on talent development, institutional support and high-performance systems.

international.headline: Indian athletes win Asian Games silver medals in squash and athletics
facts: At the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Japan, India’s Abhay Singh won silver in men’s singles squash and Anahat Singh won silver in women’s singles squash.
Ancy Sojan Edappilly won silver in women’s long jump and Sarvesh Kushare won silver in men’s high jump.
Harita Bhadra won bronze in the women’s 200 metres.
Malaysia’s Eain Yow Ng and Sivasangari Subramaniam won the respective squash singles finals.
The day’s competition was part of the 20th Asian Games, held from 19 September to 4 October 2026.
international.summary: India added individual medals in squash and athletics during the Asian Games’ 27 September programme. The results included two squash singles silvers, two athletics silvers and a bronze in the women’s 200 metres.
international.staticLink: Asian Games; international sports governance; athletics and squash
international.prelimsTakeaway: The 2026 Asian Games were hosted by Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, and were the 20th edition of the Games.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss the role of major multi-sport events in athlete development, sports administration and India’s international profile.
